### B96-F-OFFSET: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

- Kind: functional. State: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests.
- Agreement: draft: no agreement recorded.
- Method mix required by its kind: not yet measured (brief 143a). Mutation score of its bench: not yet measured (brief 143b).
- Text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
- Source: `designs/b96_kr260_10g/docs/design.md#board-result-2026-11-19-kr260-and-an-optical-loopback-resultsb96cwhw20261119_080724`

### B96-F-LEAN-GRAY-STEP: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width

- Kind: functional. State: verified; the Lean proof is of a transcription of the RTL, not of the RTL itself; rests on a delegated acceptance of the Lean statement, not a human approval.
- Agreement: draft: no agreement recorded.

- Text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.

## Limits

- Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.
- Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.
- Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.
- Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
- Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
- Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
- An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.
- 3 requirements depend on an element outside the design and have not been closed by hardware, so they hold in simulation only: B96-F-OFFSET, B96-F-INTEROP, B96-P-THROUGHPUT.
- 2 performance requirements are verified by post-route timing at one corner: B96-P-TIMING, B96-P-HOLD.
- Lean proofs here are of a transcription of the RTL, not of the RTL itself: B96-F-LEAN-GRAY-STEP, B96-F-LEAN-GRAY-DECODE.

## Reproduce

Simulation and formal evidence only; this record never lists a board, programming or deploy command.

- simulate the PCS, MAC and core against the Python reference: `python -m pytest -q designs/b96_kr260_10g/tests`
- the UVM 1.2 regression of the PCS and MAC in xsim (every test over its seeds, coverage merge, seeded bugs): `designs/b96_kr260_10g/verif/uvm/scripts/run_regress.sh --mutants --record results/112_uvm_pcs_mac`
- the pyuvm regression of the PCS and MAC in Icarus (every test over its seeds, coverage merge, seeded bugs); needs pyuvm 5.0.0 and cocotb-coverage in a venv that sees cocotb 2.0.1: `PYTHONPATH=. python designs/b96_kr260_10g/verif/pyuvm/scripts/run_regress.py --mutants --record results/123_pyuvm_pcs_mac`
- the SymbiYosys covers and proofs of the two mac64_tx interframe-gap conditions (brief 158): `bash designs/b96_kr260_10g/verif/formal/run_ifg_formal.sh /tmp/mac64_tx_ifg`
